City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 17, 2021
   In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2021-22 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 21-30 dated July 20, 2021) and California Government
  Code §53646, the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the
  City Council, City Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The July 2021
  Cash and Investment Report is presented to receive and file in accordance
  with the City’s adopted 2021-22 Investment Policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for July 2021.

  D. BUDGET UPDATE – FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 AND FISCAL YEAR 2021-22

  This report provides a budget update for the City’s General Fund and Mission
  Playhouse for fiscal years 2020-21 and 2021-22.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  E. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTIONS NO. 21-35 AND 21-36 SETTING THE RATE
  AND AMOUNT NECESSARY FOR THE 2021-22 FISCAL YEAR RETIREMENT
  LEVY

  The City’s retirement costs are funded by a special property tax levy
  authorized by the voters in 1948. The special property tax levy approved by
  the voters requires the City Council to annually establish a tax rate sufficient
  to meet the City’s obligations to the state employees’ retirement system. No
  change in the tax rate is recommended for the 2021-22 fiscal year and the
  City Council is asked to confirm the current rate and fix the amount of
  property taxes to be generated by adopting two resolutions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-35, setting
  the tax rate at 14 cents per $100 assessed valuation, and Resolution No. 21-
  36, fixing the amount of property taxes to be generated for the City’s
  employees’ retirement cost for fiscal year 2021-22.

  F. REQUEST FOR FIRST AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH LISA WISE CONSULTING, INCORPORATED (LWC) IN

  3
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 17, 2021
   THE AMOUNT OF $13,705 FOR ADDITIONAL WORK INVOLVED WITH
  PREPERATION OF THE HOUSING ELEMENT UPDATE

  The Community Development Department is requesting a First Amendment
  to an existing professional services agreement with Lisa Wise Consulting,
  Incorporated (LWC) for preparation of Housing Element Update and related
  housing programs. In late April, the State Department of Housing and
  Community Development (HCD) issued new guidelines for the suitable
  analyses for affirmatively furthering fair housing (AFFH) as a requirement for
  certification of housing elements in the 6th Cycle. For this reason, a First
  Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with LWC is required in
  the amount of $13,705 to allow for this additional required analyses.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the First Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement
  with Lisa Wise Consulting, Incorporated (LWC) for an expanded scope of
  services in the existing Agreement for completion of the Housing Element
  Update Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing Appendix; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment.

  G. ADOPTION AT SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 674 AMENDING
  CHAPTER 92 OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE TO INCLUDE
  VOLUNTARY CAT LICENSING - ADOPTION

  Ordinance No. 674 was approved at introduction by a 5-0 vote of the City
  Council at the July 20, 2021 City Council meeting. If adopted, this Ordinance
  will introduce a voluntary cat licensing option to the community, which helps
  to support animal care and control and assist in reuniting cats with their
  owners. Cat licensing and services can be expanded in the future, which can
  potentially address our community’s cat intake numbers. If adopted, the
  Ordinance would become effective 30 days after adoption.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance
  No. 674 entitled, “Amending Chapter 92 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code
  to Include Voluntary Cat Licensing.”

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 17, 2021
   H. PURCHASE OF 80 SEWER MAINTENANCE HOLE FRAMES AND COVERS
  FROM SOUTH BAY FOUNDRY, INCORPORATED AT A COST OF
  $30,922.80

  Under a provision of the March 2016 Sewer Consent Judgement with Los
  Angeles Regional Water Quality Control Board (Regional Board), San Gabriel
  is required to assess and identify issues in the sanitary sewer system needing
  repair or maintenance. City staff has evaluated the maintenance hole frames
  and covers in and around the ‘2021 Pavement Rehabilitation Project’ area and
  determined that approximately 80 are in need of replacement. The cost of 80
  maintenance hole frame and covers from South Bay Foundry, Incorporated is
  $30,922.80.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to
  approve a Purchase Order with South Bay Foundry, Incorporated in an
  amount not to exceed $30,922.80.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. PLANNING CASE NOS: GPA20-001 (GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT),
  ZC20-001 (ZONE CHANGE/SPECIFIC PLAN AMENDMENT), AND
  TMAP20-017 (TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP)
  APPLICANT: LANDWIN HOSPITALITY LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY
  SUBJECT PROPERTY: PORTIONS OF 225 WEST VALLEY BOULEVARD, 150
  HOVEY AVENUE, 152 HOVEY AVENUE, 1533 MANLEY DRIVE, AND 1535
  MANLEY DRIVE

  The proposed project is to reconfigure property boundaries of five parcels for
  the purpose of expanding an existing parking lot at the Hilton Los
  Angeles/San Gabriel Hotel. The project will require General Plan Amendment
  and Zone Change applications to change land-use designations to allow the
  parking lot use. The Tentative Parcel Map application is to reconfigure the five
  parcels.

  Recommended Action:

  The action of the City Council may be to approve, approve with modifications,
  or deny the General Plan Amendment, Zone Change/Specific Plan
  Amendment, and Tentative Parcel Map applications. Staff recommends that
  the City Council conduct the public hearing and:

  5
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 17, 2021
   1. Adopt Resolution No. 21-34 approving Planning Case No. GPA20-001,
  amending General Plan Land-Use Map from Low-Density Residential to
  Commercial Specific Plan for properties located at 150 Hovey Avenue and

  reconfiguring the parcel boundaries for 225 West Valley Boulevard, 150
  Hovey Avenue, 152 Hovey Avenue, 1533 Manley Drive, and 1535 Manley

  2. Waive full reading and introduce the attached Ordinance No. 676 by title
  only, and waive future reading; and

  3. Schedule the Second Reading and adoption of the Ordinance for the next
  regular City Council meeting. The Second Reading will require a majority
  vote of the total membership of the Council.

  Should the City Council determine the proposed project or any part of the
  proposed project be denied, the motion should be revised accordingly.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY THE HISTORIC PRESERVATION AND
  CULTURAL RESOURCE COMMISSION AND THE HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS
  AND  RELATIONS  COMMISSION  TO  CREATE  A  LAND
  ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT

  The Historic Preservation and Cultural Resources Commission (HPCRC) and
  the Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission have both
  discussed separately the development of a land acknowledgement statement.
  This report provides general information about a land acknowledgement
  statement. A Land Acknowledgement Statement is a formal statement that
  recognizes and respects the indigenous peoples as traditional stewards of this
  land, and recognizes the enduring relationship that exists between
  indigenous people and their traditional lands.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the formation of a Land
  Acknowledgement Statement Advisory Committee, allowing each
  commission to appoint their two representatives, to meet with the local tribal
  groups and develop the proposed statement.

  6
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 17, 2021
   B. ORDINANCE NO. 677 – CHANGING THE DATE OF THE CITY’S GENERAL
  MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO COMPLY WITH NEW STATE OF CALIFORNIA
  LEGISLATION – INTRODUCTION, AND RESOLUTION NO. 21-39
  APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR NOTICING REQUIREMENTS

  Following the passage of Senate Bill 970 (SB 970), it is necessary to change
  the date of the City of San Gabriel’s general municipal elections. The City
  Council will consider two options for changing the City’s current election cycle
  and the adoption of an ordinance changing the date of the City’s general
  municipal elections from March of Even-Numbered Years to either the
  Statewide Primary Election cycle or the Statewide General Election cycle
  beginning in 2022. The proposed ordinance will also adjust terms of office for
  elected officeholders. In addition, funds must be appropriated for noticing to
  registered voters in the City.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council consider the change to the City’s
  general municipal election and select one of the two options as presented
  below:

  1. Option One: Introduce for first reading by title only and waive full reading
  of Ordinance No. 677 (Version A), an Ordinance of the City Council of the
  City of San Gabriel, California, Changing the Date of the City’s General
  Municipal Election from March of Each Even-Numbered Year to the Date
  of the Statewide Primary Election of Each Even-Numbered Year Beginning
  in 2022, Adjusting Terms of Office and Repealing Ordinance No. 640-C.S.;
  and adopt Resolution No. 21-39 appropriating funds for legal-noticing
  requirements.
  2. Option Two: Introduce for first reading by title only and waive full reading
  of Ordinance No. 677 (Version B), an Ordinance of the City Council of the
  City of San Gabriel, California, Changing the Date of the City’s General
  Municipal Elections from March of Each Even-Numbered Year to the Date
  of the Statewide General Election of Each Even-Numbered Year Beginning
  in 2022, Adjusting Terms of Office and Repealing Ordinance No. 640-C.S.;
  and adopt Resolution No. 21-39 appropriating funds for legal-noticing
  requirements.
